title: Chopin, Étude Op. 25 No. 9, in three recordings
work: Étude in G♭ major, Op. 25 No. 9
question: D’Albert, Cortot and Neeman play the étude’s four-note figure as it moves through new keys and registers.
intro: The Butterfly Étude is built on a four-note figure, with detached octaves in the right hand over a leaping left hand. Chopin carries the same figure through new keys and into different registers of the keyboard. Eugen d’Albert, a pupil of Liszt, is heard here alongside Alfred Cortot and Edward Neeman.

recordings.label: Eugen d’Albert, 1912–13
recordings.note: D’Albert was Liszt’s pupil and the composer of Tiefland, an opera first staged in Prague in 1903.

recordings.label: Alfred Cortot, 1920
recordings.note: Cortot studied with Émile Decombes, who had received advice from Chopin; he later made teaching editions of Chopin’s piano music.

recordings.label: Edward Neeman, c. 2014
recordings.note: Neeman accompanied American Ballet Theatre on its 2014 Japanese tour; he also makes duet arrangements for himself and his wife, Stephanie.

passages.label: Opening four-note figure
passages.note: The right hand mixes connected notes with clipped octaves, while the left hand jumps between bass notes and chords.

passages.label: Harmonic movement
passages.note: The harmony begins to move, though the right hand keeps the four-note rhythm of the opening.

passages.label: D♭ pedal in the bass
passages.note: D♭ repeats in the bass while the right hand moves through new harmonies above it.

passages.label: Return of the opening, octave bass
passages.note: The opening figure returns with a fuller bass, the left hand now playing octaves before its chords.

passages.label: Coda over a G♭ bass
passages.note: After the loud rising passage, the bass holds G♭ and the right hand resumes its short, detached figure.
